Prevention: Sow resistant varieties because they provide the best protection against stem rust.
Balanced use of fertilizer during the crop season to ensure good health of plant.
Ensure field sanitation from barberry alternate host plants.
Spacing and field orientation away from winds coming from infected areas may protect from wind borne sources of inoculum.
Practice no tillage or minimum tillage to reduce over wintering spore inoculum.
Monitoring: Inspect wheat crops every 7 to 10 days from flag leaf emergence to early dough grain development.
Carefully inspect different plant parts, especially the lower stems, for symptoms.
Spend at least 15 minutes walking through each wheat crop.
If stem rust is detected within a region, increase inspection to every 4 to 7 days.
Look for reddish-brown, powdery, oblong pustules on the stems, leaves, glumes, awns and kernels.
If stem rust is detected, then collect 10 stems from 10 random locations (total 100) to determine the percentage of stem rust infection.

Restrictions: Check that the product is registered, and use the maximum recommended label rate for stem rust control in wheat.
Most pesticides have protective, curative, and systemic activity.
It is important to consider withholding periods when choosing an appropriate fungicide.
It is always important to read the chemical label before use and ensure protective clothing while spraying.
Avoid repeated use of fungicides with the same active ingredient in the same season.
